meta.title: Oh a Chord: press one key, get a full chord
meta.description: An iPad instrument where one key press plays a full chord. Key Mode keeps you in key; Strum, Harp and Arp turn a held chord into a part. Out now.

hero.h1: Press one key. Get a full chord.
hero.positioning: Oh a Chord is a one-octave iPad keyboard. One key press plays a full chord. Chord Type and Modifier buttons choose its quality. Key Mode keeps every note inside the key you pick. A held chord turns into a strum, a harp sweep, or an arpeggio, and never retriggers.

promise.heading: Why this exists
promise.body: Oh a Chord goes straight to the sound. Press a key and hear a chord. Hold a couple of fingers down to colour it. Key Mode keeps you inside a key without needing to know why. Most chord and arpeggiator apps want theory first: the right scale, the right extensions, an arpeggiator wired up by hand. This one asks for none of it.

features.label: One key, a full chord
features.what: A single octave sets the root. Chord Type buttons choose Dim, Min, Maj, Aug, Sus2 or Sus4. Modifiers (6, ♭7, maj7, 9, 11, 13) stack colour on top for as long as a finger holds them down.
features.why: No chord charts, no fingerings to memorize. Every Chord Type and Modifier combination resolves to a real, playable chord. There are no dead buttons mid-performance.
features.mediaAlt: The full Oh a Chord panel with MAJ selected in the Chord Type grid, the Modifiers grid below it, and the notes of the chord lit across the keyboard
features.mediaCaption: MAJ selected. The notes of the chord light up across the keyboard.

features.label: Key Mode
features.what: Arm Key Mode and the next key you press becomes the root. Every press after that stays inside that key. Reach outside it and Oh a Chord borrows a sus or diminished chord that still belongs. It never goes silent.
features.why: It's music theory you can feel rather than study. Build a progression that works before you know why it works.
features.mediaAlt: The bottom row with KEY: E lit, and dots marking the in-key notes on every key of the keyboard
features.mediaCaption: Key Mode armed on E. The dots mark what's in key.

features.label: Strum, Harp, Arp
features.what: Three independent toggles turn a held chord into a part: Strum staggers the notes like a pick across strings, Harp sweeps one or two octaves, Arp cycles up or up-and-down at the tempo you set. Latch holds the chord hands-free.
features.why: A held chord doesn't have to sit there. These are the same moves a hardware arpeggiator gives you. The notes underneath never retrigger.
features.mediaAlt: The bottom row with ARP UP and LATCH lit while the arpeggiator steps through a held chord
features.mediaCaption: ARP UP with LATCH on. The chord keeps cycling, hands-free.

features.label: A full synth underneath
features.what: Behind the gear icon sits the same 6-voice DSP core that powers Oh a Synth: oscillator, filter, envelopes, chorus. Every parameter is live and touchable. The keyboard stays where it is.
features.why: The one-key chord is the front door, not the whole house. Shape the sound as deep as Oh a Synth goes.
features.mediaAlt: The Advanced drawer open over the keyboard, showing the MAIN, LFO, DCO, HPF and VCF sections
features.mediaCaption: The Advanced drawer: MAIN, LFO, DCO, HPF and VCF, every fader live.

features.label: Save your own sounds
features.what: Tweak anything in the synth editor and a save icon appears. Tap it and name the sound. It joins the preset list next to the factory bank, stored on the device.
features.why: A good sound found by accident shouldn't be lost the next time you touch a slider.
features.mediaAlt: The preset name prompt over the settings drawer, with a lit save icon beside the close button
features.mediaCaption: The save prompt over the settings drawer. Name the sound and it joins the preset list.

download.heading: Get it
download.body: Oh a Chord is on the App Store now. It runs on iPad in landscape, iPadOS 16 or later.

rows.label: Keyboard
rows.value: Single octave; one key press plays the whole chord

rows.label: Chord Type
rows.value: Dim, Min, Maj, Aug, Sus2, Sus4

rows.label: Modifiers
rows.value: 6, ♭7, maj7, 9, 11, 13. Momentary, held while a finger is down. Combine by holding several

rows.label: Key Mode
rows.value: Locks every press to a chosen key; off-scale keys resolve to a borrowed sus or diminished chord rather than going silent

rows.label: Performance
rows.value: Strum, Harp (1 or 2 octave sweep) and Arp (up, up/down). Each is an independent toggle. Latch holds a chord hands-free

rows.label: Voicing
rows.value: Two sliders move a held chord through the register live, with no retriggering

rows.label: Synth engine
rows.value: The same 6-voice DSP core as Oh a Synth: DCO, 24 dB/oct filter, one ADSR, BBD-style chorus. Full parameter editor behind the settings gear

rows.label: Presets
rows.value: 9 factory sounds plus unlimited saved presets of your own, stored on the device

rows.label: Platform
rows.value: iPad, landscape only, iPadOS 16 or later

rows.label: Privacy
rows.value: No accounts, no analytics, no network requests of any kind. Saved presets never leave the device

items.q: Do I need to know music theory to use this?
items.a: No. That's the whole point. Press a key, hear a chord. Key Mode is there if you want to explore a key without knowing why a particular note works. It isn't required to get started.
Not yet. MIDI output is planned but not in this release. Oh a Chord is fully playable and self-contained today, with no setup.

items.q: Can I save my own sounds?
items.a: Yes. Open the settings gear and change anything in the synth editor. A save icon appears. Name it and it joins the preset list alongside the factory bank.

items.q: Does it need an internet connection?
items.a: No. Nothing about Oh a Chord leaves the device. No accounts, no analytics, no sync. Saved presets are a file on your iPad and nowhere else.
iPadOS 16 or later. It's landscape only. Chord controls sit under your left hand, keyboard under your right.
